pr_title: Fix rollback of parent destruction with nested dependent:destroy
pr_body:
### Summary

When a class has a `:belongs_to` relation with `dependent :destroy` enabled nested multiple levels doesn't delete the object if one of his children wasn't deleted.

Example:

    class User < ActiveRecord::Base
      belongs_to :user_account, dependent: :destroy
    end

    class UserAccount < ActiveRecord::Base
      belongs_to :profile, dependent: :destroy
    end

    class Profile < ActiveRecord::Base
      before_destroy prepend: true do
        throw :abort
      end
    end

    user = User.create!(user_account: UserAccount.new(profile: Profile.new))
    user.destroy

    user.destroyed? # expected: false; actual: true;

Fixes #40550

issue_context.title: Rollback of parent destruction when children association throws :abort on third level
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  gem 'activesupport', path: '../../activesupport/'
  gem 'activemodel', path: '../../activemodel/'
  gem 'activerecord', path: '../'
  gem "sqlite3"
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :users, force: true do |t|
    t.references :user_account
  end

  create_table :user_accounts, force: true do |t|
    t.references :profile, null: false
  end

  create_table :profiles, force: true do |t|
  end
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :user_account,
             dependent: :destroy
end

class UserAccount < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :profile,
             dependent: :destroy
  has_one :user,
          dependent: :destroy
end

class Profile < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_one :user

  before_destroy prepend: true do
    throw :abort
  end
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_association_stuff
    user = User.create!(user_account: UserAccount.new(profile: Profile.new))

    assert_equal 1, User.count
    assert !user.destroy
    assert_equal 1, User.count
  end
end

```

### Expected behavior

User and UserAccount should not be destroyed.
Any `DELETE`s should not be `COMMIT`ed but to be `ROLLBACK`.
`#destroy` should return `false`.

### Actual behavior

User and UserAccount is deleted from DB.
`#destroy` returns `true`.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 5.x and 6.0 (and 6.1.0rc2)
**Ruby version**: any

### Related
- https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/32376
- https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/32022
comments: An issue happens because `belongs_to` association destruction is being called after_destroy, and currently there are no way to pass `ActiveRecord::Rollback` (which is the `throw :abort` does). Current solution is to raise some other exception, like `raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid`, see more: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/33192. It will raise an error until the method caller, so you have to catch it by yourself. Would be great to fix this issue, so the thrown `:abort` `belongs_to` is going to be catched and rollback everything.
@kamipo can you please check this issue?

This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not been commented on for at least three months.
The resources of the Rails team are limited, and so we are asking for your help.
If you can still reproduce this error on the `6-1-stable` branch or on `main`, please reply with all of the information you have about it in order to keep the issue open.
Thank you for all your contributions.
I'll take a look at the issue and try to figure out a fix.

@intrip I have found that it may happen because `has_one` or `belongs_to` (can't remember) has a transaction block with empty rescue, which means `throw :abort` exception are not going to be rethrown again.

@dmitry #41602 fixes the issue, turns out was just a 1-liner.
/cc @kamipo

@intrip for some reason, if I do:

```
    before_destroy prepend: true do
      unless destroyable?
        errors.add(:base, :undeletable)
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end
    end
```

Then I can get an errors of the record afterwards.

But if I do with the fixed version and `throw :abort`

```
    before_destroy prepend: true do
      unless destroyable?
        errors.add(:base, :undeletable)
        throw :abort
      end
    end
```

I'm getting an empty `record.errors` afterwards. Somewhere it clears all the errors after throwing an `:abort`.

PS. Works as expected actually, because it throws Rollback exception.

Seems like `raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)` and `abort :about` has a different way of working. First one leaves an errors uncleared, and the second clears all the errors, because of the rollback.

@dmitry thanks for pointing this out!

I've edited the script in this issue by replacing `throw(:abort)` with `raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)` and what surprised me the most was that the exception was raised outside of the callbacks stack leading to an error, from the DOCS the `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid` error should be `rescued` automatically: https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_callbacks.html#halting-execution

I think this is also a separate issue 🤔 do you agree?
/cc @zzak @p8 

Anyways can you make new issue with a repro script? Would make much easier debugging the issue.
Also feel free to ping me in order to take a look at it when done.

I think [this](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/40550#issuecomment-879110553) is basically a docs issue, in particular [this part](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_callbacks.html#halting-execution) is not clear:

*"Any exception that is not ActiveRecord::Rollback or ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid will be re-raised by Rails after the callback chain is halted. Raising an exception other than ActiveRecord::Rollback or ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid may break code that does not expect methods like save and update (which normally try to return true or false) to raise an exception."*

It describes "ActiveRecord::Rollback" such as it works in the same way as "ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid" but actually it's incorrect: whilst "ActiveRecord::Rollback" is never re-raised "ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid" is re-raised, except for "save/update" methods.
Do you think it makes sense to make this part of the docs clearer?

/cc @p8 @dmitry

review_comments:
When `ActiveRecord::Rollback` is raised the result of `target.destroy` is `nil`. Relying on that allows to handle nested `belongs_to` with `dependent: :destroy` correctly. 
Previously `destroyed?` relied on `@destroyed` which is `true` with callbacks nested starting three or more levels.
This change also ensures that `destroyed?` returns correctly `false` in this scenario.
@intrip nice, thank you for the explanation and elegant solution. I remember that I have tried to get somehow transaction status, but gave up.
